evals.prompt: Scaffold a new deployable Python CLI application with Ruff, pytest, and GitHub Actions.
evals.expected_output: A uv-first scaffold with profile-selected runtime dependencies, a generated committed lockfile, and matching locked local and CI commands.
assertions: Uses pyproject.toml as dependency intent and uv.lock as the generated reviewed install graph
Uses uv lock --check, uv sync --locked, and uv run --locked without a parallel pip install path
Reports lock generation as pending instead of hand-authoring uv.lock when resolution was not run

evals.prompt: Add a supported runtime dependency and a development-only test tool to this published uv library.
evals.expected_output: A role-correct scoped dependency change that preserves unrelated locked packages and validates both the normal graph and declared library lower bounds.
assertions: Places the runtime package in project.dependencies and the test tool in dependency-groups.dev
Uses role-specific uv add --no-sync commands and reviews pyproject.toml with uv.lock before syncing
Keeps the normal committed lock separate from a disposable lowest-direct library test lane
Forces lower-bound re-resolution with uv lock --upgrade --resolution lowest-direct --no-sources only in that disposable lane
Does not use a broad uv lock --upgrade for the ordinary scoped dependency change

evals.prompt: Our private package index and PyPI expose the same name and uv cannot resolve the requested graph. Fix the project.
evals.expected_output: A fail-closed diagnosis that preserves resolver evidence and proposes explicit index binding without weakening source trust or exposing credentials.
assertions: Preserves uv's resolver explanation before changing dependency intent
Keeps first-index behavior and uses a named explicit index with a package source binding where appropriate
Keeps index credentials outside pyproject.toml and uv.lock
Does not widen Python support, weaken constraints, or enable an unsafe index strategy silently

evals.prompt: Harden this existing pip-tools project, but do not migrate its package manager.
evals.expected_output: A Python project hardening plan that retains the existing manager and does not introduce uv as a second lock or install authority.
assertions: Detects and preserves the existing package manager because migration was not requested
Does not add uv.lock, uv sync, or a parallel uv CI path
Still aligns relevant Python layout, test, and documentation surfaces within the requested scope

evals.prompt: Scaffold a uv-managed Python systemd service whose long-running entrypoint is acme_worker.service.
evals.expected_output: A locked deployment whose unit uses the project-owned interpreter and the explicitly generated, importable service module.
assertions: Generates an importable acme_worker.service module instead of assuming an agent.main path
Runs the module with /opt/<project>/.venv/bin/python after uv sync --locked --no-dev
Adds service arguments only when the generated entrypoint implements and tests them
Validates module importability and the rendered systemd unit

evals.prompt: Scaffold a small uv-managed Python library with configuration parsing and no external services. Keep tests meaningful and avoid unused plugins.
evals.expected_output: A minimal behavior-first scaffold with isolated unit tests and artifact verification.
assertions: Uses importlib, strict xfail and required pytest-socket without unconditional xdist
Generates no empty contract/E2E layers or pretend integration tests
Keeps normal files real through tmp_path and tests observable parser success and failures
Uses locked uv commands and a clean installed-wheel smoke check

evals.prompt: Harden a Python CLI that writes configuration files, integrates with a local database, and calls a cloud SDK. Include offline API schema contracts and an optional live workflow.
evals.expected_output: Meaningful layers, fixtures and explicit network permissions with safe CI.
assertions: Distinguishes unit, real local integration, offline contract and full E2E behavior
Runs fast local integration and offline contracts on PRs
External tests require a marker, --run-external and configured non-production target preflight; tags never enable them
Documents pytest-socket collection, teardown, subprocess and allow-host limitations
Populates required package resource assertions and tests the actual installed console entrypoint

evals.prompt: Fix a Python CLI parser bug where zero is silently accepted as a positive count. Strengthen the existing testing approach and keep the package manager unchanged.
evals.expected_output: A lowest-layer regression with meaningful boundary coverage.
assertions: Adds a parser-level regression with failing-first evidence or a concrete practical gap
Tests zero, valid and invalid counts without escalating a parser bug to deployed E2E
Preserves the existing package manager and does not add compatibility wrappers
Uses parametrization without redundant cases and asserts observable results
